title: Scan review of writing inside the twelve zodiac centres
statement: I reviewed the twelve inner centres on Yale canvases 1006200–1006207, distinguishing writing in the centre from the circumferential Voynich text. f70v2 (1006200; two fish): one Latin-script word between the fish and one freestanding Voynich word beside the upper star; the upper fish lies between that Voynich label and the Latin-script word, and no drawn line joins them. A lower star in the same centre has no label. f70v1 (1006201; horned animal at a plant): a Latin-script word on the animal; no freestanding Voynich word in the centre, and no circumferential text line immediately bounding this centre. f71r (1006202; horned animal at a plant): a Latin-script word on the animal and Voynich writing around the centre; no freestanding Voynich word. I checked this centre in a full-resolution crop. f71v and f72r1 (1006203; bull-like animals): each has a Latin-script word below the animal and circumferential Voynich writing; neither has a freestanding Voynich word. f72r2 (1006203; two figures holding hands): a Latin-script word between the figures and circumferential Voynich writing; no freestanding Voynich word. f72r3 (1006203; two clawed animals): a Latin-script word below the lower animal and circumferential Voynich writing; no freestanding Voynich word. f72v3 (1006204; four-legged animal) and f72v2 (1006204; clothed figure holding a star): each has a Latin-script word beside or beneath the emblem and circumferential Voynich writing; neither has a freestanding Voynich word. The star held by the figure is unlabelled. f72v1 (1006205; balance): a Latin-script word beneath the emblem and circumferential Voynich writing; no freestanding Voynich word. f73r (1006206; animal with looped tail): a Latin-script word beneath the animal, circumferential Voynich writing, and an unlabelled star; no freestanding Voynich word. f73v (1006207; figure with crossbow): a Latin-script word at the feet near the circumferential text; no freestanding Voynich word. In all centres with ring writing, I treated that circular line separately from a standalone label. I find no image-supported pairing of a Voynich word and a Latin-script month annotation: the sole freestanding Voynich label is next to the upper star on f70v2, with the upper fish between it and the month word. I did not transcribe or date the Latin-script words. This is a visual review, so the distinction between a ring word and a nearby centre word where they approach one another remains a judgement by eye.
check: For canvases 1006200–1006207, inspect each inner disk and record separately the writing in the disk and the circumferential Voynich line. The freestanding Voynich label occurs only beside the upper star on f70v2; there is no drawn line connecting it to the Latin-script month word. The f71r disk was checked in a full-resolution crop.
